codes.description: JSON body cannot be parsed.
Query parameters cannot be parsed or violate endpoint rules.
Parsed input does not satisfy the declared schema contract.
A required parameter is missing.
A parameter value is syntactically or semantically invalid.

A downstream service response was syntactically valid transport data but did not satisfy the expected protocol contract, including directory/projection/service-call schema mismatch or missing required pagination/error fields.
Authentication material is missing or invalid.
Session, token, or grant has expired.
Session was soft-logged-out and must be refreshed.
A soft-logout refresh, OIDC callback, re-auth, or sensitive account transition requires a fresh DID-bound or authorized-device proof; a refresh token alone is insufficient.
A required signature or proof does not verify.
Directory ingest rejected an announce or withdraw because the signed resource payload does not authorize this Directory service DID.
Directory ingest rejected the resource because it is outside the directory's advertised accept policy.
Directory ingest rejected a resource governance proof because its detached signature is invalid or cannot be canonicalized.
Directory ingest rejected a signed payload because its as_of timestamp is outside the configured freshness window.
Directory ingest or cross-service projection could not verify declared source_refs against the authoritative principal server, resource source, or signed projection frontier.
Directory ingest rejected a governance proof because the signing key is not valid for the resource DID document's current epoch.
A service-call TTL is outside the operation's allowed range, including directory ttl_seconds outside [1, max_ttl_seconds] or ephemeral ttl_ms beyond the advertised kind-specific limit.
Directory ingest rejected an announce because an active withdrawal or operator takedown blocks acceptance of the resource.
Directory ingest rejected an announce because policy_revision or as_of is older than the indexed entry.
Capability, policy, or visibility rules deny the request.
The target Realm is frozen, archived, tombstoned, or otherwise closed to ordinary writes.
A required claim, attestation, or presentation is missing.
A realm-level policy refuses the requested write or fanout (read-receipts §2.5: cx.receipt.read drops when disclosure='disabled'; retry_after_ms is null because retry will not change the outcome).
cx.ephemeral.send rejected the envelope because the actor lacks the kind-specific broadcast capability or Realm policy disables that ephemeral kind.
cx.ephemeral.send rejected ttl_ms because it is absent when required or outside the service's advertised kind-specific range.
cx.ephemeral.send could not enqueue or fan out the transient signal because the ephemeral channel is temporarily unavailable; durable Event history is not affected.
The target does not exist or is not visible to the requester.
The path is inside the protocol namespace but not implemented by the service.
The path exists but the HTTP method is not supported.
A generic state conflict occurred.
An optimistic concurrency precondition failed.
Causal dependencies, prev_refs, refs[role=authorized_by], or actor-chain constraints are violated.
A required dependency is missing and may be recoverable via backfill or retry.
The target Flow discussion track is disabled.
The referenced encryption epoch is stale or unavailable.
The same idempotency key or stable identifier was reused with different canonical content.
No valid fractional rank exists between the requested bounds; a rebalance or different position is required.
The producer cannot allocate a fresh HLC logical counter in the current millisecond without violating monotonicity.
The request or blob exceeds declared size limits.
A declared digest does not match the transferred content.
Encrypted envelope AAD digest does not match the canonical normalized AAD.
Encrypted payload digest does not match the declared encrypted envelope content.
Required encrypted content key, MLS epoch, or authorized key share is not currently available.
Encrypted content or MLS epoch is bound to an application state root that cannot be verified against accepted state.
An auditable E2EE decrypt receipt was invalidated by backfill, witness, or state verification.
A DID cannot be resolved or validated under the active resolver policy.
Storage, bandwidth, or compute quota was exceeded.
The caller exceeded the current rate limit policy.
A wait-for, long-poll, or upstream dependency timed out.
The service frontier is behind the causal frontier required by the request.

A federation high-assurance peer has missed proactive frontier probes or produced invalid/divergent frontier evidence and is quarantined for the affected Realm until fork resolution succeeds. See zh/sync/federation.md §4.5.3.
The opaque cursor (cx:cursor:...) has a valid shape but its `x` expiry is in the past. Client MUST request a fresh cursor (initial /account/subscribe, /snapshot/head, or new write barrier).

Cursor integrity check failed: MAC / signature did not verify, the bound transcript (principal, device, service, filter_hash, purpose, positions, target, x, issuer_kid) did not match the authenticated request, or the stateful handle is unknown / revoked / cross-bound. Distinct from cursor_expired (TTL) and cursor_unrecognized (cross-service portability miss). Client MUST clear local cursor cache and restart from initial /account/subscribe.
A required protocol feature is not supported.
The service does not accept the requested active standard Event kind.
The requested projection cannot be claimed complete under the current supported feature set or dependency frontier.
An internal service error occurred.
The service is temporarily unavailable or cannot currently satisfy the request.

The submitted Realm policy combination (discoverability × join_rule × history_visibility) violates the v1 normative compatibility matrix in zh/discovery/discovery-directory.md §3.1. Reducer keeps the prior accepted state.
Realm create rejected: anchor_profile=single_did was declared without a recovery_anchorer in a different controlling organization, in violation of zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.
The implementation does not support a lattice type referenced by the Realm schema (e.g., lww-register or rga without cx.profile.collaborative_text.v1). Receivers fail closed.

Caller requested an operation that relies on a Realm-declared profile or feature this service has not declared in cx.server.describe.supported_features / supported_profiles. The server MUST fail-closed and MUST NOT silently downgrade to a permissive interpretation.

Reducer state-machine precondition failed. Carried with a reason_code in the {flow,space,morph,message,relation}_not_active / _not_archived / _already_terminal family, or with object-specific reasons like space_parent_cycle. See zh/models/common-fields.md §5.1.
The hash algorithm prefix in a typed hash value (e.g. cx:event:<algo>:<digest>) is not in the receiver's supported hash list. See zh/conformance/encoding.md §3.2.
Anchor frontier has gaps within the receiver's auth_chain backfill bound; soft-fail per zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md.
E2EE frank cannot be produced for the requested ciphertext (sender did not include franking sidecar). See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §3.4.
TURN REST-style ephemeral credential is past its TTL; client MUST request a fresh credential. See zh/crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §6.1.
Federation sender used an obsolete member delivery binding frontier; response carries new_recipient_service_did and handover_frontier so the sender can retry at the current service.
Federation sender continued using a previous recipient_service_did after the handover grace window expired; sender MUST resolve the current binding and retry there.
Idempotency cache replay is served only as a historical diagnostic after key or binding state changed; receivers MUST NOT perform new reducer side effects.

reason_codes.description: Sentinel value indicating an item or decision succeeded with no further reason.
Event was rejected because the active capability constraint requires approval evidence (per zh/authz/capabilities.md §6 / §8) and none was supplied.
No active capability grant authorises cx.message.create on the targeted Flow track for the actor.
The capability grant cited as authority was revoked at a frontier causally preceding this event; reducer rejects.
Concurrent grant/revoke ordering cannot be deterministically resolved with currently available history; recipient SHOULD backfill or escalate to manual review rather than picking a winner.
Service is not in the Realm's plaintext_visible_services policy; plaintext-bound operation refused.
A previously valid Read-Your-Writes receipt has been invalidated by subsequent backfill, witness disagreement, or audit_assurance mismatch (see zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §4).
Two distinct canonical-byte events share the same event_id; reducer MUST quarantine and require operator action (see event-auth-state-resolution.md §11).
Local state does not match the authoritative frontier; client SHOULD reconcile via backfill or snapshot before continuing.
Item was placed in quarantine pending operator decision (state_conflict_resolution); not finalized.
Auth state for the event could not be fully resolved within the implementation's auth_chain backfill bound; treat as soft-fail per scalability-constraints.md.
Required refs[role=authorized_by] are not yet accepted at the local frontier; the event MUST be parked until the missing refs converge.
Projection cannot be materialized because of missing reducer inputs, decryption_pending epochs, or out-of-window backfill.
Recipient cannot decrypt the targeted MLS epoch yet; client MUST surface a placeholder and continue retrying within the configured window.
Recipient permanently cannot decrypt; epoch is unrecoverable on this device under current keys.
Implementation does not advertise the feature requested; caller SHOULD downgrade or pick another peer.
Event kind is not active in the receiver's profile or registry; receiver MUST NOT silently drop, MUST report this code.
Event kind does not appear in any known registry entry; treat per non_critical_extension_rule (preserve canonical bytes, ignore in reducer) unless declared in critical_extensions.
Bytes are not valid Contrix canonical JSON (sorted keys, integer-only numbers, escape rules per encoding.md §1).
Generic encoding violation (HLC format, UUIDv7 format, base64url alphabet, etc.) not otherwise classified.

Cursor payload fails the §8.2 / §8.3 cursor syntax or schema before integrity verification. HTTP endpoints surface this as top-level `invalid_param` with reason_code `invalid_cursor`. Expiry uses `cursor_expired`; MAC/signature/cross-binding failures use `cursor_integrity_invalid`; cross-service portability misses use `cursor_unrecognized`.

Cursor decoded successfully but cannot be translated by this service because it is a stateful handle issued by another service or the receiver does not support stateless cursor reparse. This is a cross-service portability miss, not TTL expiry and not local integrity failure; caller MUST restart sync from a fresh cursor.
Cursor's `x` expiry is in the past; caller MUST request a fresh cursor.

Cursor failed the §8.3.1 integrity check: stateless `_mac` / `_sig` did not verify against the issuing service's current cursor key, or transcript binding (principal / device / service / filter_hash / purpose / positions / target / x / issuer_kid) did not match the authenticated request; or stateful `h` handle is unknown / revoked / cross-bound. Distinct from cursor_expired (TTL) and cursor_unrecognized (cross-service portability miss). Triggered before any server-side state advancement (to-device ack, /account/subscribe after= resume, X-Contrix-Wait-For release, dropped/resync_required recovery). Client MUST clear local cursor cache and restart from initial /account/subscribe.
Standard moderation reason: spam content.
Standard moderation reason: harassment.
Standard moderation reason: hate speech / targeted attacks against a protected group.
Standard moderation reason: not-safe-for-work / explicit adult content posted outside permitted contexts.
Standard moderation reason: content alleged to violate applicable law (CSAM, threats, IP infringement, etc.).
Standard moderation reason: misleading / false information posing harm.
Standard moderation reason: catch-all for reports that do not fit the named categories. MUST be accompanied by a free-text `description` field. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §3.2.
Multiple reports clustered together for triage; not finalized.
Cross-Realm abuse network signal aggregated by moderation server.
Awaiting moderator review.
A policy-server-issued recall of a previous allow decision; corresponding action MUST be reversed if still reversible.

Snapshot inclusion / omission challenge failed: issuer could not produce a valid Merkle branch or ordered-set slice for a sampled Event ID / actor sequence range against the manifest's event_set_commitment.root, OR the proof's root differs, OR an actor sequence gap is not reflected in soft_failed/quarantined digests. Client MUST quarantine or reject the snapshot and fall back to raw Event replay.

Snapshot signer's authority (Realm owner / admin / trusted snapshot issuer / witness quorum membership) was revoked at or before the manifest's `created_at`, or revoke freshness cannot be confirmed within the verifier's max_anchor_staleness_ms. Client MUST quarantine or reject the snapshot. A revoke that takes effect strictly after `created_at` does not retroactively invalidate a previously valid snapshot.

Federation push / pull body's service_binding_ref.reducer_profile_hash differs from the receiver's reducer profile for the target Realm. Receiver MUST reject the entire batch (not partial-accept) because the same Event under different reducer profiles would produce divergent cell state, state_root and covered_frontier — silently accepting would corrupt audit. Sender SHOULD reconcile reducer profile via Realm policy update or terminate federation for this Realm.

HTTP Message Signature @authority / target URI host does not match the resolved service endpoint for Destination-Service-DID, or the Destination-Service-DID is not authorized by Realm policy for the requested federation operation. Receiver MUST reject before processing events.

Resource selector or constraint exceeds parser hard limits defined in resource-selector-grammar.md §3.3 (string length, resources[] length, token count, nesting depth, single-field length, requires_claims item count, constraint nesting). Distinct from invalid_param so audit / abuse-detection can separate suspected parser-DoS attempts from ordinary format errors.

Cross-method principal upgrade (e.g. personal_node `did:web` -> small_team `did:webvh`) is missing the OOB fingerprint confirmation evidence or any of the required `transfer_evidence` fields (key-management.md §5.0.5).

Cross-method principal upgrade `cx.did.proof.continuity` `signature_chain` is missing one of the two mandated signatures (old-method inception key + new-method entry-0 controller key) or one of the signatures fails to verify (key-management.md §5.0.5).

Cross-method principal upgrade evidence `old_did_document_canonical_hash` does not match the receiver's canonicalised view of the current `old_did` DID Document. Indicates the hosting domain has been substituted after the upgrade was signed (key-management.md §5.0.5).

Cross-method principal upgrade evidence `inception_pubkey_fingerprint` does not match the fingerprint derived from `verificationMethod[0]` of the canonicalised old DID Document (key-management.md §5.0.5).

An `attested_hardware` audit profile removed an Audit Agent without the enclave-signed epoch key destruction attestation required by audited-e2ee.md. The Audit Agent is treated as still holding historical epoch keys; the Realm MUST drop the `attested_hardware` claim and surface a downgrade banner.

An attested_hardware Audit Agent was removed via cx.mls.commit but the same anchor batch lacks the required cx.audit.epoch_key_destruction attestation. Reducer MUST reject the batch (audited-e2ee.md §3.1.1.3).
cx.audit.epoch_key_destruction carries an `enclave_measurement` that does not match the Audit Agent's join-time attestation. Indicates the enclave image was swapped before destruction.
cx.audit.epoch_key_destruction `epoch_range` does not cover the full range of epochs the removed Audit Agent is known to have held secrets for.
cx.audit.epoch_key_destruction proofs[] do not chain to the enclave / HSM attestation key; only enclave-internal attestation keys are accepted.
cx.audit.epoch_key_destruction `remove_commit_ref` points to a cx.mls.commit that is not in the same anchor batch as the attestation.
An event violates a declared relation / cell cardinality constraint.
Atomic claim of a one-time key / pre-key / KeyPackage failed because it was already consumed, revoked, or not present (crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md KeyPackage claim path).
Realm declares both cx.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1 and cx.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1; these are mutually exclusive (encryption-and-audit.md §2.4.2).
Realm attempts to set mls_send_pause='advisory' without declaring cx.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1; default profile MUST treat mls_send_pause as a MUST gate.
`cx.flow.archive` / `cx.flow.update` rejected because the target Flow is not in `active` state (per zh/models/common-fields.md §5.1).
`cx.flow.restore` rejected because the target Flow is not in `archived` state.
A `cx.redaction` event targeting a Flow is rejected because the target Flow is already in terminal state `redacted`. Flow terminal state is reached via cx.redaction.
`cx.space.archive` rejected because the target Space is not in `active` state (per zh/models/realm-and-space.md §3.3).
`cx.space.restore` rejected because the target Space is not in `archived` state; `tombstoned` is a terminal state and MUST NOT be restored.
`cx.space.tombstone` rejected because the target Space is already `tombstoned`.
`cx.space.parent` would create a cycle in the Space ancestor chain (self-loop or chain loop). Reducer MUST reject (zh/models/realm-and-space.md §3.5).
`cx.morph.archive` / `cx.morph.update` rejected because the target Morph is not in `active` state.
`cx.morph.restore` rejected because the target Morph is not in `archived` state.
`cx.redaction` targeting a Morph is rejected because the target Morph is already in terminal state `redacted`.
`cx.message.redact` / equivalent rejected because the target Message is already `redacted` or `deleted`.
`cx.relation.delete` rejected because the target Relation is already `tombstone`.

A previously trusted cross-signing key set was reset; verifications against the old `ssk_generation` MUST fail until the user re-verifies under the new generation. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.

A `cx.cross_signing.reset` proof was signed by a key class that does not have authority for that proof.kind: `principal_signing.signed_by` is not a principal-grade DID control key (or is the self/user signing key being retired), `recovery_unlock` is signed by a key that is not the declared recovery key, `trusted_recovery_service` is signed by a non-published verification method, or `device_quorum.signatures[i].signed_by` is not the named device's authorized key. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4.

A `cx.cross_signing.reset` proof signature failed verification: `principal_signing.signature` does not verify under the resolved principal-grade DID control key, `recovery_unlock` / `trusted_recovery_service` signature does not verify under the bound key, or any `device_quorum.signatures[i]` does not verify under the named device key. Key-class or authority failures use `cross_signing_reset_proof_authority_invalid`. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4.

`cx.cross_signing.reset.previous_generation` does not equal the receiver's currently accepted publish generation, or `new_generation != previous_generation + 1`. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4.

`recovery_unlock.recovery_secret_ref` does not resolve to a recovery key declared in the principal's current DID Document recovery section / `recovery_policy` at `issued_at`. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4.

`recovery_unlock.unlock_commitment` does not equal the receiver-recomputed `SHA-256(utf8('cx-cross-signing-reset-unlock-binding-v1\n') || recovery_secret_ref || unlock_binding_input_bytes)`, where `unlock_binding_input_bytes` is the §14.1 canonical input with `proof_body` excluding both signature fields and `unlock_commitment`. This is a wire-integrity binding (not a secret-knowledge proof) preventing the same recovery-key signature from being shelled into a different reset envelope. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4.
After deduplication by `device_id` and signature verification, `device_quorum.signatures[]` contains fewer than `threshold` valid signatures. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4.

`device_quorum.threshold` is below the principal's currently published `recovery_policy.device_quorum.threshold`; receivers MUST reject so issuers cannot weaken the quorum unilaterally. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4.

`trusted_recovery_service.service_did` is not declared in the principal DID Document recovery section or organization `recovery_policy.trusted_services[]`, or is outside its validity window. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4.

A `trusted_recovery_service` declaration requires an `attestation_ref` but the proof omits it, or the ref does not resolve to a verifiable attestation event. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4.
`cx.cross_signing.reset.issued_at` deviates from receiver local clock by more than `cx.profile.cross_signing.reset.v1.max_clock_skew_seconds`. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4.

Another `cx.cross_signing.reset` already consumed the same `(principal_id, previous_generation)` tuple; receivers MUST reject duplicates until the corresponding successor `cx.cross_signing.publish` is accepted + 24h. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4.
Proof / event signature `alg` is not in the conformance signature-algorithm allowlist. See zh/conformance/encoding.md.

Per-(requester, target, intended_realm_id) KeyPackage / one-time-key claim rate limit hit; caller MUST back off before retrying. Distinct from the global `rate_limited` HTTP code because the limit is keyed on the (target, intended use) tuple, not the caller alone.

A registry entry (event_kind / schema_id / typed-id) violates the canonical naming convention (e.g. embedding a `.v<n>` version suffix in the kind name instead of carrying the version via `requirements.features`). Surface as lint output, not as a wire-time reject.

An approval signature carrying a (approver_did, nonce) tuple that was already consumed for the same grant_id / proposal_id was resubmitted. Approval signatures are single-use per-grant; reusing them is a cross-grant replay attempt. See zh/authz/constraint-schema.md §9.3.

An Event whose envelope signature was produced by an applet / delegated agent key but whose `actor_id` points to a different (native) principal DID is missing the mandatory `executed_by` / `authorization_ref` / `applet_id` fields. Reducer MUST schema_violation per zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §11.

A 3PID invite claim arrived with the invite_token sourced from a URL query string or path segment instead of from a URL fragment or out-of-band code, in violation of zh/sync/third-party-invites.md §3.2. The verification service MUST reject and SHOULD invalidate the token to prevent referer / log replay.

A `cx.patch.v1` patch path violates the ABNF grammar in zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4.2.1 (malformed identifier, non-canonical selector-value, ambiguous quoting, path > 1024 bytes, or nesting > 16 segments). Parser MUST NOT attempt fallback recovery; reducer rejects with this reason.

A single payload.patch contains parent/child writes, duplicate target paths, selector-affecting writes, or another multi-path combination that cannot be applied as one deterministic atomic Move. Reducer MUST reject the whole patch rather than partially applying paths. See zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4.4.

A `cx.patch.v1` patch path attempts to modify a reducer-managed field (`id` / `schema` / `realm_id` / `created_by` / `created_at` / `state` / `state_changed_at`). These fields are owned by their corresponding lifecycle events; patch MUST NOT touch them. See zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4.2.5.

A `cx.patch.v1` `$op="unset"` was used on a redactable content field (e.g. message.content, flow.summary, encrypted_payload). Redaction MUST go through `cx.<kind>.redact` or `cx.redaction` events to enforce redaction-specific capability checks and audit. See zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4.2.4.
A `cx.patch.v1` selector segment matched zero array items for a `set` or `add` operation. See zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4.2.3.

A `cx.patch.v1` selector segment matched multiple array items, indicating the underlying collection already violated its declared uniqueness constraint. Reducer fails closed. See zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4.2.3.

An AEAD-encrypted payload (encrypted_payload, blob attachment, to_device, etc.) repeated a per-(key_ref, epoch, device_id) counter already seen by the receiver. The receiver MUST reject the payload before AEAD decryption to prevent attempted nonce reuse against a valid sender device. See zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md §3.1 and zh/conformance/encoding.md §10.1.

An AEAD nonce on the wire does not match the deterministic derivation from MLS-Exporter context {key_ref, epoch, purpose} plus (device_id, monotonic counter) mandated by zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md §3.1. Producers MUST NOT emit naive random nonces under shared MLS application keys; receivers MUST reject such payloads to enforce the cross-implementation nonce-uniqueness contract.

An Actor Profile update declares an `accountable_to[]` entry without a corresponding active `cx.identity.accountability_grant` (issuer=that DID, subject=profile.principal_id, grant_status=active, within validity window). Deployment policy chooses between (a) reducer reject with this reason, or (b) silently strip the unverified entry from the resulting profile + emit audit log. See zh/models/actor.md §3.3.1.

An MLS Welcome arrived with a `claim_envelope` whose canonical signing input does not match the Welcome's actual intended_realm_id / claim_id / requester_did, or the envelope signature does not chain to the Welcome sender's self-signing key. See zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.6.

A `cx.capability.delegate` would close a cycle in the delegation graph (when traversed by grant_id node DFS). Reducer MUST reject the entire delegation chain to prevent circular authority. See zh/authz/capabilities.md §10.

A delegated grant's `expires_at` is later than the parent grant's `expires_at`, or `not_before` is earlier than the parent's `not_before`. Delegation MUST NOT widen the parent's validity window. See zh/authz/capabilities.md §10.
Conflict-recovery Move is missing the required `refs[role=state_witness]` reference. See zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §8.1.
Conflict-recovery Move's inclusion proof cannot reconstruct the witness's `state_root`. See zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §8.1.

Conflict-recovery witness frontier has a causal path from one of the sibling Moves that triggered the bottom — i.e., the witness is not strictly pre-conflict. See zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §8.1.
Conflict-recovery witness's state_root does not contain (or contains a divergent value for) the recovery_capability cell referenced by the grant. See zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §8.1.

A runtime challenge proof attached to `cx.member.state{join}.gate_proofs[]` or `member.application.gate_proofs[]` (candidate kind, no `cx.*` prefix) fails verification (signature / freshness / verifier domain). See zh/authz/policy-server.md §4.

A child grant or Move depends on a parent grant that is locally known to be revoked, superseded, expired, or tombstoned. Reducers MUST fail closed without waiting for the child causal frontier to include the revoke. See zh/authz/capabilities.md §10.3.

A capability grant's normalized effective validity window is empty: effective_not_before >= effective_expires_at after combining top-level valid_from/valid_until with temporal not_before/expires_at constraints. Reducer MUST reject the grant. See zh/authz/capabilities.md §6.1.

The account status frontier contains a deactivation for the principal acting as actor, subject, issuer, recipient, or device owner. New device/session grants, KeyPackage operations, capability delegation, delivery binding writes, push routes, and to-device enqueue MUST fail closed. See zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md §7.1 and zh/sync/federation.md §4.4.1.

The referenced moderation state cell is in bottom / exposed multi-head conflict. Read, write, distribute, and policy-check paths MUST fail closed rather than selecting a temporary winner. See zh/authz/policy-server.md §7.2.

`cx.mls.welcome.payload.claim_ref.capabilities_digest` does not match the claimed KeyPackage capabilities, or the Welcome requires capabilities outside the claimed subset. Receivers MUST reject before decrypting the Welcome. See zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.6.

Reading the full per-Flow watch state (including `muted` entries) requires both `cx.realm.notification.audit` and `cx.audit.accessed` capabilities; one was missing. See zh/models/flow-and-message.md §8.5.

`cx.flow.watch.set` may only set the watch state of the submitting actor; cross-actor writes require `cx.flow.watch.manage_others` (audit / accessibility scope). See zh/models/flow-and-message.md §8.4.

`cx.flow.watch.set` writing `level="muted"` for another actor is rejected — `muted` suppresses mention / moderation / workflow notifications and MUST be opt-in by the target actor themself. `cx.flow.watch.manage_others` only authorizes writing `level ∈ {mentions_only, participating, all}` for other actors. See zh/models/flow-and-message.md §8.4.

`cx.flow.watch.set` writing `level_public=true` for another actor is rejected — publishing one's own subscription level is an opt-in personal disclosure and MUST be written by the target actor themself. `cx.flow.watch.manage_others` writes MUST omit `level_public` or set it to `false`. See zh/models/flow-and-message.md §8.4.

A `cx.flow.watch.set` write that uses `cx.flow.watch.manage_others` to set another actor's watch state was rejected because it lacked refs[role=audit_pair] to a same-batch `cx.audit.accessed` event, or the paired audit payload did not identify the same writer DID, target actor DID, cell id, paired event id/digest, and before/after heads. See zh/models/flow-and-message.md §8.4.

A structural `contains` Relation was submitted that would cross Realm boundaries. Structural containment (Board → List → Flow / Space hierarchy) MUST stay within a single Realm; cross-Realm links use the dedicated `cx.relation.*` non-structural kinds. See zh/models/relation.md §4.

A `cx.member.state{membership=join}` event's `join_authorisation` proof (the equivalent of Matrix `join_authorised_via_users_server`) does not verify against the cited reviewer's capability state at the citing frontier. See zh/governance/join-policy.md §6.

Realm `cx.realm.join_rule` and `cx.realm.policy_components` declare conflicting join modes (e.g., `restricted` with no gate configuration, or `knock_restricted` with all-auto gates degrading to `restricted`). See zh/governance/join-policy.md §4.
`cx.space.tombstone` cannot proceed because the target Space still has active `contains` Relations or non-tombstoned child Spaces. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md §3.4.
A bounded-lifetime artefact (member application, reservation cell, presign envelope, runtime gate proof, etc.) is past its declared `expires_at` / TTL window. See per-feature spec sections.

The requested principal / service / Realm is recognised by the registry but no provisioning exists at this endpoint — caller should bootstrap or pick another host. See zh/sync/service-http-binding.md.

cx.morph.update attempted to modify schema_refs[] without going through the Realm's declared schema-evolution policy (high-tier capability such as cx.morph.schema.migrate, or equivalent) and an explicit audit-grade authorization_ref. See zh/models/morph.md §4.1 S2.

cx.morph.update attempted a non-additive schema_refs[] transformation (breaking or transformation-class change). Such transformations MUST be expressed as a cx.morph.schema_migrate event and require the Realm to declare the cx.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1 opt-in profile. See zh/models/morph.md §4.1 S3.

A reducer-input event targeting an evolvable-schema object (typically a Morph) did not include the active schema profile id(s) in requirements.schema[]. Reader cannot resolve which schema version to validate the event against. See zh/models/morph.md §4.1 S1 and zh/models/event-and-patch.md §2.7.

An event declared cx.profile.franking.sender_commitment.v1 in signed requirements.features[] but the unsigned.franking.sender_commitment sidecar was absent when plaintext-level sender attribution was requested. The message may remain valid as a core E2EE event, but sender attribution MUST fail closed. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §3.4.2.

A reporter-submitted sender commitment sidecar digest did not match the signed payload commitment, or its tag did not verify against the recomputed HMAC under the derived Sender Commitment Key. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §3.4.2.

A sender_commitment (sender_device_id, epoch, epoch_local_seq) seq was already present in the persisted seen-set for that (sender_device_id, epoch). See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §3.4.2 step 3.

The ciphertext_digest bound in the sender_commitment does not match the digest of the encrypted envelope the reporter submitted; cannot attribute plaintext to the claimed sender. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §3.4.2 step 4.

The MLS epoch bound in the sender_commitment does not match the envelope's sender_claim.epoch; commitments are per-epoch and MUST NOT be carried across epochs. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §3.4.2 step 5.

A cx.attestation.range_completeness attestation's root (payload schema cx.schema.range_completeness_attestation.v1) does not match the locally-recomputed Merkle root over the scope's reducer-input events. Indicates either silent omission by the issuer or scope/canonicalization drift. See zh/sync/operations-sync.md §4.2.4 step 4.

Verifier's local actor view contains a per-actor seq gap inside an interval that a cx.attestation.range_completeness attestation (payload schema cx.schema.range_completeness_attestation.v1) declared complete. Most likely indicator of silent fork or partial replication divergence beyond the attestation's stated scope. See zh/sync/operations-sync.md §4.2.4 step 6.

A cx.realm.policy_components write under cx.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1 declared relaxed_window_max_ms greater than the spec hard ceiling (300000 ms / 5 min). Reducer MUST reject the policy update and receivers MUST NOT silently clamp; otherwise visible policy state splits across implementations. See artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json#cx.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.downgrade_window_constraint.

A deployment attempted to enable cx.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1 alongside a compliance-tier profile (cx.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1 / cx.profile.disclosed_audit.e2ee.v1 / any audit_assurance >= disclosed_policy). The relaxed window contradicts the compliance presumption that kick-out is cryptographically immediate; the combination MUST be rejected by the reducer. See artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json#cx.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.downgrade_window_constraint.compliance_profile_disabled.

A cx.cross_signing.reset payload declared a trust_domain that does not match the receiver's own trust_domain (or the receiver is unable to validate that the declared trust_domain belongs to this deployment). Rejected before signature verification to prevent replay of reset proofs across deployments / sovereign trust domains. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.1.

cx.cross_signing.reset payload's reset_event_id does not match the enclosing Event Envelope's event_id. Binding reset_event_id into proof transcript prevents wrapping the same proof bytes into a different Event shell; receivers MUST reject the reset on any mismatch. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.1.

A cx.moderation.appeal.decision event with verdict=overturn was anchored without a paired cx.moderation.decision.lift event in the same Anchor batch (targeting the original decision_ref). Reducer MUST reject; appeal overturn is only complete when the lift is observed atomically. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5.2.

The reviewer in cx.moderation.appeal.review / cx.moderation.appeal.decision is the same actor who issued the original cx.moderation.decision being appealed. Separation of duties forbids self-review; reducer MUST reject. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5.

Realm has accepted cx.realm.destroy (or equivalent terminal decommission marker) and cannot accept new ordinary writes. Only audit-class events (cx.audit.*, cx.audit.erasure_receipt) are still acceptable. Receivers MUST reject cx.events.submit for any other kind targeting this Realm. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.5.

Audit Agent's join-time attestation evidence (cx.schema.attestation_evidence.v1) measurement does not match the enclave_measurement recorded in cx.audit.epoch_key_destruction. The two share root of trust; mismatch indicates code / policy_version drift between join and destruction. Reducer / verifier MUST reject. See zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §3.1.1.2.

Audit Agent's attestation_evidence.audit_purpose does not match the Realm policy's declared audit_purpose at join time. Verifier MUST reject the Welcome; the Audit Agent MAY re-attest with the correct purpose. See zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §2.

Requested operation targets a blob / object currently under legal hold. cx.blob.presign / cx.blob.delete / redaction-equivalent operations MUST be rejected with this code; legal hold takes precedence over capability and TTL. See zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md §5.4.4.1.

Blob has been redacted (cx.redaction accepted) or hard-erased (cx.audit.erasure_receipt published) and is no longer fetchable. Both new presign requests and in-flight (not-yet-expired) presign URLs MUST be rejected with this code. See zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md §5.4.4.1.

An SFU / MCU attempted to negotiate plaintext-decrypting media role without being listed in Realm policy plaintext_visible_services[] with purpose=media_plaintext, OR without policy_root covering media_service_decrypts=true. MUST be rejected; the SFU may still act as opaque RTP relay. See zh/crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §10.3.1.

Current MLS epoch's governance binding policy_root does not cover the Realm policy components the client wants to act on (e.g. media_service_decrypts toggle, plaintext_visible_services). Receivers MUST refuse to act until a fresh commit updates policy_root. See zh/crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §10.3.1 and zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §3.2.
Invite token's expires_at has passed when claim is attempted. Internal-only reason code; the wire response MUST be the unified non-enumerable `not_found` per zh/sync/third-party-invites.md §6.1.

A late-arriving key tried to upgrade a decryption_failed event to late_recovered, but the receiver was not a member of the Realm at the original causal time T₀ (or has since been banned/removed). Client MUST NOT admit the recovered plaintext to verified timeline; audit log records this code. See zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.6.1.
